answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity anchor. Each agent posts a hashed commitment, waits a full epoch, then reveals the key behind it; only revealed identities older than the waiting period may attest or earn. Picture a mesa above a lagoon: the plateau is the set of mature identities, and nothing climbs onto it quickly. An attacker who wants a thousand sybils must park a thousand commitments early, pay the bond on each one, and keep them alive through the whole delay, so the velvet-smooth instant swarm that sybil attacks rely on becomes a slow, expensive, visible queue.
